newsitem.title: GERMANY: Austria not satisfied with EU Iran decision.
newsitem.headline: Austria not satisfied with EU Iran decision.

text.p: Austrian Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel said on Wednesday he was not satisfied with an agreement by European Union states over relations with Iran, saying he would have preferred some kind of economic sanction.
"I would have liked more substance in the decision," Schuessel told Berlin broadcaster Inforadio. "I would have liked us to have been harder in the economic sphere."

EU foreign ministers agreed in Luxemberg on Tuesday that ambassadors from the 15 member states could return to Tehran if their governments wished, but suspended ministerial ties with Iran in response to a court finding that Iranian leaders had ordered political assassinations in Germany.
Schuessel said it was important that EU countries spoke with a united voice on the issue or they risked being played off against each other.
He also stressed the importance of Iran's geographical position and oil reserves and said it was therefore important that the EU continued dialogue at government level.
